seo_title: SEBI: All FPIs Now Deemed Accredited Investors
title: SEBI Revises Accredited Investor Framework, Deems All Foreign Portfolio Investors Accredited
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India
case_name: Review of the Framework for Accredited Investors
card_summary: SEBI's November 5 circular revises the Accredited Investor framework under the amended AIF Regulations, 2012. Every person resident outside India under FEMA, including all Foreign Portfolio Investors, is now deemed an Accredited Investor without a separate certificate, though the manager must record the basis for treating them as such. An LLP can also qualify if every partner meets the criteria.
card_tip: A foreign investor or FPI investing through an AIF or PMS no longer needs to apply separately for accredited status, though the manager must record the basis for the deemed status and ordinary KYC obligations continue.
verification_notes: The circular's date (November 5, 2026), its number, the deeming of persons resident outside India and FPIs as Accredited Investors, the manager-led assessment, and the LLP eligibility change are reported consistently by Lakshmikumaran & Sridharan and Compliance Calendar, and the circular itself is available on sebi.gov.in. The reported Rs 5 crore securities-exposure threshold appeared in only one secondary source in this run and is therefore not stated as a confirmed figure here.
